targets.title: The Missing Link Between Parents’ Preferences and Daughters’ Survival: The Moderator Effect of Societal Discrimination
targets.evidence_quote:
Data-analytic replication attempt to evaluate a claim from Echávarri_WorldDev_2016_YmQR
Replication team: Bob Reed, Jianhua Duan, Nathaniel Porter, and Sanghyun Hong
SCORE RR ID: 69412
OSF Project: https://osf.io/c6pkb
Claim evaluation
Single-trace claim
Coded claim 4 text (original paper): “Regarding the effect of societal discrimination against young girls, holding constant other socioeconomic and cultural factors, and given the mean number of unwanted daughters within the household (0.80), our estimates support that increases in societal discrimination are associated with 0.045 increases in the expected number of daughters’ deaths (p < 0.001).”
targets.outcome_quote:
Results 1 (without sampling weights): This claim was replicated. The marginal effect of societal discrimination on daughter’s mortality rate (the coefficient on societal discrimination, SD) is .0279747 and its p-value is less than 0.000.
Results 2 (with sampling weights): This claim was replicated. The marginal effect of societal discrimination on daughter’s mortality rate (the coefficient on societal discrimination, SD) is .0203866 and its p-value is less than 0.000.

reasoning: Assigned OSF GUID resolves to the complete SCORE claim report, with matching Echávarri/Husillos citation and team members Duan, Porter and Hong; OSF contributor names include Parsons and Miske. Report explicitly judges the target claim replicated both with and without weights. Classified as replication because the report identifies NFHS 2015-16 secondary data for a paper whose DOI dates to 2015, suggesting a later sample; the report does not explicitly compare original and replication sample waves, so record-type uncertainty remains. This is not evidence that original numerical output was rerun. The 2026 supplied year differs from the OSF file creation in 2022, but file identity is unambiguous.
